newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices rise on fresh mill demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices rise on fresh mill demand.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Monday rose on fresh demand from mills, dealers said.
Limited inflows and a shortage of ready stock kept offerings at a low ebb.

In spot deals Bengal-deshi jumped up by 40/50 rupees at 985/1,050 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned rose by 10 rupees at 1,810/1,840 rupees per maund and F-414 by five rupees at 2,050/2,075 rupees per maund.

Gujarat varieties too gained on fresh mill demand. Gujarat wagad rose by 300 rupees at 13,000 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while Kala-ginned moved up by 300 rupees at 12,300 rupees per candy. Kalyan cotton however held steady at 14,000/14,300 rupees per candy.
"Fresh arrivals in the producing centres remained low due to the tail end of the season but some of the state-owned agencies are having enough unsold stock with them," one broker said.
"If cotton prices go up further, these agencies may unload this stock," he said.
